Thank you very much, Mr. President. For me, it's an honor to present this National Voluntary Report of the Dominican Republic to everyone present here this afternoon. This is an effort by not only the Minister of Planning and Development, but also many different state institutions. And the private sector and civil society also. This report presents the progress we've made on 9 SDGs, and it contains 80 indicators for the 2021 to 2024 period and has benefited from information both from the SDG follow-up system as well as statistical databases and national surveys. And it's also been complemented thanks to information on the different policies that are being engaged in, in different public and private institutions. 113 different governmental and non-governmental initiatives have been adopted. And there has been an effort made to have disaggregated data disaggregated in different categories like gender, territory, and also different groups of vulnerable populations. A lot of emphasis during this period has been placed on aligning planning instruments and budgetary instruments with the Sustainable Development Goals. When it comes to the first SDG, that's SDG 1, ending poverty, we have made some really significant progress in the Dominican Republic. We've managed to reduce monetary poverty to 19% in 2024, and that's the lowest level on record. That's the lowest level we've had in history. We managed to not go above the level due to the pandemic, and we've actually managed to go down to pre-pandemic levels now. And this is shown not only in monetary poverty indicators but also in indicators on multidimensional poverty. Nevertheless, we do see poverty persisting among several groups including women and in some more economically disadvantaged regions. Key policies to achieve this have been the continuation of conditional monetary transfer programs, housing programs, and employment programs. We still have the challenge of expanding access to opportunities to goods and services, in particular for our most vulnerable populations. When it comes to SDG 3, that's health, we've managed to make significant progress. In the teenage pregnancy rate, reducing it by 52— from 52% to 36%, and also a decrease in teenage pregnancy in general. It's gone from 21% to 28%— to 18%, rather. Nevertheless, we are continuing to make efforts on this issue. However, the policies that have been implemented have managed to achieve some significant progress. Furthermore, we have a high level of coverage of health insurance. That's 97%, although we are aware that we need to continue to improve the functioning of the health system. To achieve this, the National 2030 Health Program has been adopted. We also have a national digital health strategy, and we have strengthened the care that we are providing to groups of persons with HIV/AIDS and other groups. We have the early care and treatment system for cancer. On gender equality now, we have made notable progress reducing family violence as well as violence against women. There has been a sustained decrease in both rates, and we've also improved access to women in the, in the House, the lower chamber of the legislature. Last year's elections, we saw an increase in participation. It went up to 36.6% from the 24% it was before. So we are aware that there's still a significant gap that we need to continue to work to narrow. We've also worked on preventing early marriage. We've adopted a law— passed a law to prohibit child marriages, and that's also had an effect on teenage pregnancy. We also have hotlines to help to prevent violence against women. When it comes to public finance systems, we have implemented a classification system for public expenditure with a gender focus where we've been able to identify the different expenditure that's being engaged in for gender. So when it— and also looking at public procurement with a gender focus. When it comes to the SDG on decent jobs and employment. SDG 8, we've managed to sustain a growth rate of 5% since the pandemic per year, also a reduction in disemployment of 5%. And a challenge remains improving access to formal employment. We still have a lot of informal employment. However, income from labor has increased between 2021 and 2024. So that's part of the explanations that explain why and how people are improving their level of income, and also how we've achieved the increase— the decrease in poverty that I mentioned earlier. The amount of young people that are in study or work has maintained stable. We have also a difference in employment based on gender, and women are more disadvantaged than men here. Nevertheless, we have been reducing the gap over recent years. When it comes to reductions in inequalities, we've made progress here. Especially in the Gini Index, there's been a 7% reduction. There's also been some convergence in terms of the difference between rural and urban areas, achieving better territorial cohesion. The Human Development Index also increased from 3.1% between '21 and '24, and we've also seen a 21% increase when we adjust, adjust it for inequality. And this is the lowest rate we've had since 2016. Here I wanted to mention the cohesion policies that have been implemented. We've adopted laws On organizing the territories and planning, this is part of the focus of our government on the regions, that is adopting public policies that benefit people to reduce the gaps that we see throughout the country. When it comes to sustainable production and consumption, The most significant progress that we've made has been the 37% increase in the installation of renewable energy and also efforts made by companies to recycle waste. 15% of companies are telling us that they're recycling their companies are recycling their waste and 1,616 have responded, for example, on solid waste and have a sustainable procurement program. On life underwater, 79% of the marine areas in the country are under a new protection regime and that's in line with the 30 for 30 initiative. 900 square kilometers of wetlands have been protected as well as large swathes of coastal areas. We've been collecting oceanic data and engaging in monitoring and the country is also engaged in a significant fight against sargassum. We've created the National Cabinet to fight against sargassum and drafted a contingency program for sargassum that has enabled us to better manage and mitigate this issue. When it comes to SDG 16, strengthening strong institutions, our country has made notable progress in the Corruption Perceptions Index. That's an 8%— rather, an 8-point improvement, and we've gone up 33 positions since 2020. When it comes to reducing violence, we've had a 13.2% reduction in the homicide rate since 2021. It's gone to 11% in 2024. We're seeing a high rate, though, still among young men. A challenge is improving the amount of persons that have been arrested who have not faced trial. That's still a challenge. When it comes to SDG 17 on alliances, the country has shown a growth in foreign investment. and also the announcement of the Plan Mita, which is an initiative of the Dominican Republic to duplicate GDP by 2036, so to double it. And it's an initiative where the public and private sector are participating, and the private sector is proposing initiatives that require the government to take actions also so that we can increase our growth rate by a percentage point and double GDP by 2036. I'd like to underscore the participation, like was mentioned before, of the public and non-governmental sectors with 47 initiatives, public institutions, 66 initiatives from non-governmental organizations, and I'd like to particularly underscore the participation of the private sector, of companies that is benefiting also from the support of the UN system, implementing sustainable companies, reducing your footprint. Among the measures that we've implemented, The country, like I mentioned before, has returned to a 5% level of growth, and we're implementing the National Comprehensive Framework for Financing for Development. And we are also part, with the Seychelles, of the implementation of financing for small island developing states. As part of this initiative, we've earmarked a public budget for the SDGs, and for 2024, 96% of the budget was aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.
